acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner's minor son is residing with her. She has filed a petition under Section 125 Cr.P.C. and an FIR under Sections 406, 498-A IPC at Chandigarh. Respondent-husband has filed a petition under Section 13(1)(ia)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act at Panchkula to harass the petitioner.

legal_principles.principle: While deciding the transfer application, courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of female litigants.
legal_principles.held: The Courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of the female litigants and transfer of legal proceedings from one Court to another should ordinarily be allowed, taking into consideration their convenience and the Courts should desist from putting female litigants under undue hardships.
cited_cases: Rajani Kishor Pardeshi Vs. Kishor Babulal Pardeshi, (2005) (12) SCC 237

legal_principles.principle: The cardinal principle for exercise of power under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.
legal_principles.held: The cardinal principle for exercise of power under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

legal_principles.principle: In matrimonial matters, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both parties, their social strata, behavioural pattern, standard of life prior to and subsequent to marriage, and circumstances of both parties in eking out their livelihood.
legal_principles.held: In matrimonial matters, wherever Courts are called upon to consider the plea of transfer, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

legal_principles.principle: When two or more proceedings are pending in different Courts between the same parties which raise common question of fact and law, and when the decisions in the cases are interdependent, it is desirable that they should be tried together by the same Judge.
legal_principles.held: Further, when two or more proceedings are pending in different Courts between the same parties which raise common question of fact and law, and when the decisions in the cases are interdependent, it is desirable that they should be tried together by the same Judge so as to avoid multiplicity in trial of the same issues and conflict of decisions.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, (2022) Live Law (SC) 627
keywords: common question of fact and law

outcome.final_order: The court allowed the transfer application and transferred the case from the Family Court, Panchkula to the competent Court of jurisdiction at Chandigarh.

use_for_drafting: assisting with transfer of petitions between courts
